skill.name: amedas-weather
skill.description: Retrieve recent weather observations from JMA AMeDAS stations across Japan, including temperature, humidity, wind, rainfall, and available pressure readings.
skill.summary: Read current Japanese weather observations with station names and observation times, without an API key.
skill.author: tahodev

security_audit.summary: All 21 static findings are false positives in context: Markdown backticks, public JMA endpoints, a documentation link, and readable multilingual text. The documented commands retrieve weather data and process station coordinates locally; no evidence of credential access, exfiltration, destructive behavior, or prompt injection was found. This assessment covers the supplied SKILL.md, not the unavailable linked documentation.

content.value_statement: Weather forecasts do not show what nearby stations have just measured. This skill guides assistants through public JMA observations with station names and timestamps.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve the latest JMA observation timestamp and construct the corresponding observation download URL.
Read available temperature, humidity, wind, rainfall, sunshine, and pressure values from station observations.
Resolve station codes to names, coordinates, and elevations using the public station table.
Find an approximately nearest station using a Python example and supplied coordinates.
Report observation times in JST and identify the station used.
Handle retrieval failures and missing measurements with explicit explanations and official fallback information.
limitations: Provides observations, not forecasts, rain radar, or weather warnings.
Measurements update every ten minutes, and available elements differ between stations.
Requires network access and curl; the nearby-station example also requires Python 3.
The proximity example uses squared coordinate differences, and the referenced shared response checklist is not included.

use_cases.title: Check Nearby Conditions
use_cases.description: Read recent temperature, humidity, wind, and rainfall measurements for a nearby Japanese station before a commute.

use_cases.title: Summarize Local Measurements
use_cases.description: Prepare a timestamped observation summary for a field team, with missing measurements clearly identified.

use_cases.title: Inspect Public Weather Data
use_cases.description: Explore station metadata, measurement availability, and quality flags when preparing a weather data analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Check One City
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the latest available temperature and humidity for Tokyo. Include the station name and observation time in JST.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request a simple current observation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Rain and Wind
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the latest wind and one-hour rainfall near Osaka. Identify the station, units, observation time, and any unavailable measurements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: request several measurements with clear intervals.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Nearby Station
prompt_templates.prompt: Use coordinates 35.68, 139.77 to find an approximately nearest AMeDAS station. Report available weather measurements with the station name and JST timestamp.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: select a station using geographic coordinates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Station Observations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Tokyo and Yokohama observations at the latest shared timestamp. Include available temperature, humidity, wind, rainfall, quality flags, and station names.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare stations while preserving data quality context.

output_examples.input: Show an example observation summary for Tokyo.
output_examples.output: Historical example from the skill: Tokyo station 44132, September 20, 2026, 13:20 JST. Temperature: 22.8 C. Humidity: 92%. Past 24-hour rainfall: 15.0 mm.

output_examples.input: What should you report if the selected station has no pressure measurement?
output_examples.output: This station does not provide pressure observations. I can check a nearby station that measures pressure and identify its location and observation time.

output_examples.input: What should you report if JMA data remains unavailable after retries?
output_examples.output: AMeDAS observations could not be retrieved. Current conditions are unknown. Please check the official JMA disaster information page.

best_practices: Use the retrieved latest timestamp, and include the station name and observation time in every summary.
Check measurement availability and quality flags before interpreting values, especially for sensitive decisions.
Run downloads in a dedicated working directory to avoid replacing existing amap.json or stations.json files.
anti_patterns: Do not describe observations as forecasts or predictions of future conditions.
Do not treat missing measurements or retrieval failures as zero values or clear weather.
Do not present historical examples as current observations or omit rainfall accumulation periods.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The documented JMA endpoints provide public data without an API key or login.

faq.question: Does this skill provide weather forecasts?
faq.answer: No. It covers observations. The instructions refer forecast requests to the separate jma-weather skill.

faq.question: How frequently are observations updated?
faq.answer: The instructions describe ten-minute observation intervals. Always check and report the timestamp returned by JMA.

faq.question: Why are some measurements missing?
faq.answer: Stations measure different weather elements. Pressure is available only at some stations, and absent keys should not be interpreted as zero.

faq.question: How does the skill select a nearby station?
faq.answer: The Python example converts station coordinates to decimal degrees and minimizes squared coordinate differences. This is an approximate proximity calculation.

faq.question: What software and access are required?
faq.answer: The download examples require curl and network access to JMA. The nearby-station example also requires Python 3 and a downloaded station table.
